**Why no run the old code committed can move (PLAUSIBLE, by the code):** the two conditions differ only for a hole the
kernel made at or over the sliver area that the clean leaves under it. The old code kept such a ring in
`provedRings`' result and proved it; if the proofs passed, `partsOf` (`polygons.ts:241`) dropped it by the same
cleaned `|area2|`, so the body is the same; `proveRings` judges ring by ring and pair by pair, so a ring fewer cannot
fail where the fuller list passed; `provedRings`' result has the one reader (`keep`, through `partsWithSeeds`). Only
a run the old code refused on such a ring can change — it now commits.

## Judgments (vetoable)

**K8 survives, and it is not equivalent — at one value.** `<=` in place of `<` differs for a hole the clean leaves at
exactly the sliver area (a cleaned `|area2|` of exactly 80 000, i.e. 40 000 cm²): the code keeps and proves it — "a
hole the clean leaves at or over 4 m²", and `partsOf` keeps it by the same strict `<` — and K8 drops it before the
proofs, an islet of exactly 4 m² lost from the body. `probes/zz-crafted.test.ts` under K8 (`probes/crafted-K8.out`)
shows the one difference: the plain 250 cm × 160 cm hole 12 cm off the outer ring is `not clear (rings meet)` on the
tree's code and "kept 1 ring" under K8; every other case equal. No pin of the folder carries a hole of exactly that
area (the crafted ones are 39 200 and 40 800 cm²; S4's pockets 3.3 m² and 5 m²). **Why not a blocker, in this lane's
reading of the rule** ("a survivor on a stated promise you do not find equivalent stays a blocker"): the tree's code is
right at the value (CONFIRMED by the probe: it agrees with `partsOf`); what is missing is one more pin, at a single
lattice area between the two the round pins — "a further hardening test, a tightening of a claim" of the brief's rule
(3), fail-safe in both forms (a typed refusal, or a commit without an islet of 4.0000 m²; N-45), on nothing persisted.
The required change's own pin list (the two crafted holes, S4's three cases) and its five mutants are met in full. It
is the same footing as K9 / K10 at the S4 check, on a band narrowed from a few per cent to one value. Recorded as
N-s5c-1 (M4: one assertion — a plain clockwise rectangle of exactly 40 000 cm² 10 cm off the outer ring is refused
`rings meet`). **A veto by the session fails the item on that line.**

**K9 survives; judged equivalent on every ring whose winding the clean keeps.** The code reads "hole" from the ring
the kernel made (`area2(r) < 0`); K9 reads it from the cleaned ring (`area2(c) < 0`), which is how `partsOf` sorts
outer rings from holes (`polygons.ts:242`). The two differ only for a ring whose winding the clean REVERSES while
leaving it under the sliver area (or leaves at zero area with three or more vertices): `cleanRing` removes vertices
within 20 cm of a chord and never reorders them, so a reversal needs a ring thinner than the tolerance that the clean
folds over itself — a ring `proveRings` then refuses `not simple`, or `partsOf` drops under the sliver area whichever
way it winds. No such ring was constructed, and none is met (every pin and all 91 tests agree). Under either reading
no ring the body keeps is dropped unproved (both test the cleaned `|area2|`). Recorded as N-s5c-2 (M4: a comment or a
pin; the "one measure" of the round is the AREA's, the winding is still the kernel's).
